title: Angkor Wat
subtitle: Cambodia's Iconic Wonder & World's Largest Ancient Temple
shortDescription: The heart of Cambodia and the world's largest ancient temple complex.
overview: Built in the early 12th century, Angkor Wat is Cambodia's proud national symbol. Originally constructed as a Hindu temple for Lord Vishnu, it later became a sacred Buddhist sanctuary. Its iconic five lotus towers represent Mount Meru, the center of the universe in ancient tradition.
highlights: Watch a breathtaking sunrise over the central lotus towers reflected in the front lily ponds.
Explore grand stone wall carvings telling ancient stories and epic historical legends.
Discover over 1,800 detailed carvings of celestial Apsara dancers throughout the galleries.
Climb up to the central top tier sanctuary for amazing 360-degree views of the jungle.
practicalInfo: You will need an Angkor Pass to visit. Please dress respectfully by covering your shoulders and knees, wear comfortable walking shoes, and bring a hat and sunscreen!

title: Bayon Temple
subtitle: The Famous Temple of 216 Smiling Stone Faces
bestTime: Nov – Feb (Late afternoon for golden light on stone faces)
shortDescription: Famous for its 54 stone towers decorated with giant, peaceful smiling faces.
overview: Built in the late 12th century by King Jayavarman VII, Bayon stands right at the center of the ancient walled city of Angkor Thom. It is world-famous for its 54 towers bearing 216 giant smiling stone faces carved into the rock, representing peace, kindness, and royal wisdom.
highlights: See 216 gentle, smiling stone faces looking out in every direction.
Explore detailed wall carvings showing daily village life, markets, and ancient boat battles.
Walk through stone hallways, towers, and hidden passages inside the temple.
Visit in the late afternoon for warm golden sunlight on the smiling expressions.
practicalInfo: Included with your Angkor Pass. Located inside Angkor Thom, just a 5-minute drive north of Angkor Wat.

title: Koh Rong & Sanloem
subtitle: Tropical Islands with White Sand & Clear Blue Water
bestTime: Nov – May (Calm turquoise seas & bright sunshine)
shortDescription: Crystal-clear waters, soft white sand beaches, and magical glowing plankton at night.
overview: Located off the coast of Sihanoukville in the Gulf of Thailand, Koh Rong and Koh Rong Sanloem offer 43 kilometers of soft white sand beaches, clear turquoise waters, colorful coral reefs, and bioluminescent plankton that glow in the ocean at night.
highlights: Relax on soft white sand beaches like Sok San Beach, Long Set Beach, and Saracen Bay.
Take a night boat trip to swim with blue glowing plankton under starry skies.
Snorkel and dive along healthy coral reefs filled with colorful tropical fish.
Hike short jungle paths leading to quiet waterfalls and hidden beach coves.
practicalInfo: Speedboats run daily from Sihanoukville (takes about 45 minutes). Please use reef-safe sunscreen to help keep ocean life safe!

title: Preah Vihear Temple
subtitle: Ancient Clifftop Temple Overlooking the Plains
bestTime: Nov – Mar (Clear morning skies for mountain views)
shortDescription: A majestic temple perched on a high mountain cliff with incredible views across the country.
overview: Perched dramatically on a 525-meter cliff in the Dângrêk Mountains, Preah Vihear is a magnificent UNESCO World Heritage site dedicated to Lord Shiva. Built over 400 years by succession of Khmer kings, this mountain temple stretches 800 meters along the cliff ridge.
highlights: Walk up an impressive 800-meter stone pathway passing through five grand stone gates.
Enjoy sweeping 360-degree views from the top cliff edge overlooking the plains below.
Admire beautifully preserved stone carvings telling ancient stories.
Experience a peaceful mountain atmosphere far away from crowded tourist spots.
practicalInfo: Bring your passport for a quick entrance check. Local 4WD vehicles or motorbikes are available at the base to take you up the steep hill.

title: Tonle Sap Lake
subtitle: Southeast Asia's Largest Lake & Unique Floating Villages
bestTime: Aug – Feb (High water season for flooded forest boat rides)
shortDescription: Discover unique floating communities, stilted villages, and rich birdlife.
overview: Tonle Sap is the largest freshwater lake in Southeast Asia and a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve. Twice a year, the river reverses its flow, expanding the lake four times bigger and creating rich water habitats for local floating communities.
highlights: Visit unique floating villages like Chong Kneas and tall stilted homes in Kampong Phluk.
Spot rare water birds like pelicans at the Prek Toal Bird Sanctuary.
See floating schools, markets, pagodas, and fish farms adapting to changing water levels.
Enjoy a relaxing boat ride to watch the sunset across the open water.
practicalInfo: August to February is the best time for boat trips through the flooded mangrove forest. Joining local community tours directly supports resident families!

title: Bokor Hill Station
subtitle: Cool Mountain Air, Historic Ruins & Coastal Views
bestTime: Nov – Apr (Cool mountain breeze & clear coastal views)
shortDescription: A cool mountain park featuring historic French colonial buildings and sweeping sea views.
overview: Located 1,000 meters above sea level within Preah Monivong National Park in Kampot, Bokor Hill offers pleasant cool weather, misty rainforests, and historic French buildings from the 1920s overlooking the sea.
highlights: Explore the historic Le Bokor Palace hotel and old French Catholic church.
Visit Wat Sampov Pram temple for spectacular cliffside views of the ocean.
See Popokvil Waterfall and enjoy refreshing mountain hiking trails.
Enjoy cool, refreshing temperatures away from the lowland heat.
practicalInfo: The weather on the mountain is cooler, so bring a light sweater or jacket! It is an easy 45-minute scenic drive up from Kampot town.

title:
Tuol Sleng
(S-21)
subtitle: A Historic Memorial & Museum of Resilience
shortDescription: A former school turned memorial museum, preserving history to educate future generations.
overview: Originally a high school, this site was converted into Security Prison 21 (S-21) during the 1970s. Today, it stands as a solemn museum preserved in its original state to educate visitors, preserve history, and honor memory.
highlights: Listen to an informative audio guide featuring personal stories from survivors.
See preserved classrooms, historic photo displays, and original records.
Visit the quiet courtyard memorial stupa for prayer and peaceful reflection.
Meet living survivors and learn about Cambodia's inspiring journey of healing.
practicalInfo: Please dress modestly and speak quietly out of respect. We highly recommend getting the audio guide at the entrance to learn the full history during your visit.

title: Cardamom Mountains
subtitle: Cambodia's Great Rainforest & Wildlife Sanctuary
bestTime: Nov – Mar (Dry season hiking & wildlife tracking)
shortDescription: One of Southeast Asia's largest rainforests, rich in wildlife, rivers, and waterfalls.
overview: Covering over 4.4 million hectares, the Cardamom Mountains are one of the largest intact rainforests in Southeast Asia. This vast green sanctuary protects wild elephants, rare birds, and pristine river networks while supporting community ecotourism.
highlights: Stay with local villagers in eco-friendly communities like Chi Phat and Stung Areng.
Enjoy jungle river kayaking, mountain biking, waterfall trekking, and wildlife safaris.
Stay in peaceful eco-lodges surrounded by lush rainforest nature.
Explore dense green forests filled with wild orchids, gibbons, and tropical birds.
practicalInfo: Always hire a trusted local guide for safety when hiking in the forest. Remember to bring bug spray, good walking shoes, and water!

title: Royal Palace
subtitle: The Official Home of Cambodia's King & Sacred Golden Treasures
shortDescription: A grand palace complex featuring traditional Khmer golden roofs, gardens, and the Silver Pagoda.
overview: Built in 1866, the Royal Palace is the official home of King Norodom Sihamoni. Located right along the river in Phnom Penh, this stunning landmark features traditional Cambodian golden roofs, beautiful gardens, and the world-famous Silver Pagoda.
highlights: Walk on a floor paved with over 5,000 real solid silver tiles.
See the famous Emerald Buddha and a solid gold Buddha covered in over 9,500 sparkling diamonds.
Explore the majestic Throne Hall with its high 59-meter spire, used for crowning Cambodian kings.
View historic royal clothes and traditional artifacts from Cambodia's rich history.
practicalInfo: Please dress respectfully by covering your shoulders and knees. Photos are not allowed inside the Silver Pagoda. We recommend visiting in the morning to enjoy cooler, pleasant weather!

title: Banteay Srei
subtitle: The Citadel of Women & Masterpiece of Stone Carvings
bestTime: Nov – Feb (Early morning 7:30 AM for warm pink light)
shortDescription: A beautiful pink sandstone temple famous for its extraordinarily detailed stone carvings.
overview: Built in 967 AD, Banteay Srei translates to 'Citadel of Women', named for the delicate beauty of its stone artwork. Crafted from rose-pink sandstone, this compact temple features some of the sharpest and most detailed stone wall carvings in ancient Khmer history.
highlights: See masterpiece pink sandstone carvings depicting famous ancient legends.
Enjoy a quiet, intimate temple layout surrounded by lotus-filled water ponds.
Admire remarkably preserved goddess statues carved directly into the stone walls.
Learn about temple restoration efforts at the modern visitor center near the entrance.
practicalInfo: Included with your Angkor Pass. Located about 45 minutes north of Siem Reap—easy to combine with a visit to the nearby Landmine Museum!

title: The Killing Fields
subtitle: A Peaceful Memorial Garden for Reflection & Peace
shortDescription: A quiet memorial site dedicated to honoring history and promoting peace for the future.
overview: Choeung Ek was a major historical site in the late 1970s. Today, it has been transformed into a peaceful memorial park dominated by a tall glass Buddhist Stupa, surrounded by quiet green trees and orchards.
highlights: Visit the central Glass Memorial Stupa created to honor victims and promote peace.
Follow a gentle self-guided audio walking path around the peaceful memorial grounds.
Visit the small museum exhibit to watch documentary films and learn about peace initiatives.
Walk along quiet orchard paths designed for peaceful thought and reflection.
practicalInfo: Please dress modestly and speak quietly out of respect. Conveniently reached by tuk-tuk or ride-hailing app from central Phnom Penh.

title: Yeak Laom Lake
subtitle: Clear Emerald Volcanic Lake Surrounded by Jungle
bestTime: Nov – Apr (Crystal clear emerald swimming conditions)
shortDescription: A clear, circular crater lake hidden in the jungle of Ratanakiri.
overview: Formed over 700,000 years ago by a natural volcano, Yeak Laom is a clear circular lake surrounded by lush green jungle. Located in Ratanakiri, this peaceful spot is protected and cared for by the local indigenous Tampuen community.
highlights: Swim in clear, fresh emerald waters while listening to peaceful jungle sounds.
Walk along the shaded 3km path that loops around the entire crater rim.
Visit the Tampuen Cultural Center to see traditional crafts and musical instruments.
Discover colorful butterflies, birds, and tropical plants along the water's edge.
practicalInfo: Please swim only from designated wooden docks to respect local community rules. A small ticket fee at the entrance supports local village conservation!
